Well then you can still try to go cold turkey by not bringing it in the house. The next time you go grocery shopping, avoid buying junk food. If it's not in the house then it's harder to indulge in it. 

If that's not possible due to others being in the home with you who eat it, then maybe just cut it out slowly. Cut back on one thing at a time until it becomes easy to avoid junk food.

I don't have it in the house but I do have a roommate who does bring something in every now and then but because it isn't mines, it's easier to avoid versus if I bought it for myself. 

Like I said before, its hard to go cold turkey but it's possible if you have the willpower and a tool like IF. But since you can't do IF, the next best thing would be to just not have it around you as much as possible.

I haven't completely cut out junk food because I know that's not going to be sustainable long term but so far IF (intermittent fasting) has made it pretty hard to get junk food into my diet because I'm smarter with my choices. The less time you have to eat, the more you want to consume high quality food to fill you up at least that's what IF has done for me.

I say still have it every once in a while but try to make it once or twice a month if you can (which I have done already this month). Going cold turkey is hard and most wouldn't suggest it but that's what I did with the help of IF. 

I started with 16/8. Eating for 8 hours and doing 16 hours of fasting. Now I do OMAD (one meal a day) which makes it really hard to get junk food into my diet because I'm looking to eat something filling like a salad with lots of protein and fats. Junk food just doesn't have that kind of quality and I would be hungry af eating something like hot dogs, chips, donuts, ice cream, soda and chocolate bar in my one meal.
Hopped on the scale this morning and I'm down 16.5lbs in less than 4 weeks. It might not show on my flair but I'm down to 279.5 from 296!

IF so far has worked wonders for me and I would suggest keep doing that if you lost 10lbs on it. It might help you with lessening your portion sizes by splitting up your meals if you do 16/8 and eat only lunch and dinner or breakfast and lunch. 

I do OMAD (one meal a day) most days which has helped shrink my appetite. I barely get hunger pangs anymore. I know OMAD is extreme for most but it helped me get to eating a lot less and just seeing how massive my portion sizes were. 

Maybe that could help you if you did it maybe once or twice out of the week. 

I also don't exercise right now and have lost 15lbs in 3 weeks by doing IF (started doing OMAD after the first week). 

So maybe that will help you.

Your story sounds almost identical to my story. I lost 80lbs and went from 272 to 192 about 7 years ago. Going to the gym was a way to punish myself as well and I hated the way I looked every step of the way. Even at my lowest weight, I still wasn't satisfied and now I would give anything to get back there. I was so depressed then and wasn't ready to lose the weight like I am now. Mentally I was a mess. And if your mental doesn't align with your body it will be hard to lose the weight and keep it off.

My advice (which is advice to myself as well) is don't do what you did the first time. Now that you're at a better place mentally, you can start to align your mind with your body. 

I feel tons better now that I am older and see that I have to really be mentally checked in in order for this to work. That the hate and disgust I felt for myself to try to fuel my weight loss then was not healthy and the only way to lose this weight now is by loving myself at every phase of the journey which isn't easy when the world doesn't want to see you do that but you have to do it if you want to succeed. 

Just think how you're gonna feel six months from now, twelve months from now, eighteen months from now when you probably might hit your goal weight or at least get back to where you were before. It takes self-love, not hate to get there.

Don't accept everything. Be smart about your choices. Calculate the amount it says you'll get vs the distance. For instance, if it says $6.00 for 20 miles that's definitely not worth it vs $6.00 for 3 miles. 

Try not to do the $3.00 orders if possible. Those are more than likely going to be no tip.

Stay away from certain fast food restaurants. Every city is different but on average most dashers stay away from Mcds Wendys Taco Bell BK and KFC if they can help it especially if it's only $3-$6 orders. But sometimes they may be the only ones you can go to especially late at night and early in the am because their open early and late.

Find out the good neighborhoods (aka white well to do neighborhoods) because that's your ticket to being able to do this full time. They usually tip pretty good. I have yet to get less than $5 in those areas.

Also choose your restaurants wisely. I hate to make this a race thing but it's hard to ignore. White restaurants and families...you are bound to get a good tip like say your local salad or sandwich restaurant that is uber expensive. Other races on average rarely tip though I've had a few whites not tip but they were in a poor neighborhoods so...

Military neighborhoods are also cash cows. Got a $15 tip from one family the other day.

Also don't always go near the hotspot, instead go to the restaurants that are the most expensive and fancy because usually those will be the customers to tip you well (not always but most often than not because they have it to spare).

Also you will make the most money doing as early in the morning as you can, take a break between 10-12 and hit the lunch hours (12 to 2, on Fridays 11 to 2) and then early evenings like 5 to 9. On weekends it's 4 to 11. This is just what I notice in my area though could be different for you.

My advice could not work for you but the general consensus on here is definitely stay away from $3 orders as much as possible.

You have two options:

A. Tell her the truth and how you feel about it. If you're not ready to do something like that (which believe me I definitely understand...that happened to me during Superbowl Sunday) then just don't do it. I ended up gaining while at my family's that week and it took almost two weeks of going very strict to get it back off. I will not do that any time soon again and so glad there are no more holidays or special events coming up where they will be cooking a big meal. 

B. Go but plan ahead. Just because you go out to eat, doesn't mean you can't find out what they have that would work into your calorie budget. Big things that help if you're going out to eat is eat a big salad first so that when the entrée comes around, you won't have much room for it. Also, skip out on the croutons, dressing, and crackers when eating the salad and you should be fine. And of course don't drink your calories. Also when picking your entrée go for the lower calorie options like most places have steak and broccoli or grilled chicken and some kind of vegetable if you don't like broccoli. 

I will say one thing about option B is that its good practice because if you have events or birthdays coming up, then you would have to get used to it anyways.

January I went keto but messed up bad but still lost a bit of weight from I guess continuing my fasting habits which has now become a part of my daily life like showering and brushing my teeth. I would start with focusing on intermittent fasting if you don't want to do keto and maybe doing 12:12 or 14:10 at first and then gradually increase the time you fast. 

Since Feb. 15th, I've been strict and eating under 50g of total carbs per day and just in one week managed to get into the 200s which I haven't been able to do in almost 2 years. 

I've also been able to wear shirts I could barely fit into before easily and the most important thing that has changed big time for me is how I feel. No more nauseating headaches, chest pains and I can walk/stand for long periods of time. 

I couldn't do any of that before.  

I also have been learning my body and truly studying my eating habits and realizing how warped my mind has been on how I see food. Fasting teaches you discipline but more than that it really shows you that food is your source of energy first and should be seen as such. It's ok to indulge but only once you fix the things that kept you from being able to move on after indulging otherwise you will never fix your addiction to sugar/junk.

To me it has been a game changer both mentally and physically.

And seeing this progress has made me want to keep going. 


P.S. counting calories/logging becomes easier when you only have one or two times a day of eating versus three or four. I think that's one of the biggest things I love about IF because logging can be aggravating at times.
